title: Approximation of a local map into a completed stalk
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$, $y\in Y$ lie over $s\in S$. Assume that $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Let $\theta:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$ be a local $\mathcal O_{S,s}$-algebra homomorphism, where the completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every integer $N\geq1$, there are an etale morphism $p:U\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $u\in U$ with $p(u)=x$ such that $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field], and an $S$-morphism $f:U\to Y$ with $f(u)=y$, such that for every $a\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ the elements $\widehat p^{\sharp}(\theta(a))$ and $\iota_u(f_u^{\sharp}(a))$ differ by an element of $\mathfrak m_u^N\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$. Here $\widehat p^{\sharp}:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$ is the map on maximal-adic completions induced by $p$, $\iota_u:\mathcal O_{U,u}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U,u}$ is the completion map, and $\mathfrak m_u$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, lemma-map-approximation, statement and proof at lines 11017–11068; Artin approximation input is Smoothing Ring Maps Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant.

proof.text: The assertion is local on X, Y, and S. Choose affine neighbourhoods S=Spec(R), X=Spec(A), and Y=Spec(B) containing s, x, and y, and write x and y as primes p of A and q of B. Put r=p intersected with R and replace R,A,B by their localizations at R\r; then R=O_{S,s} is a G-ring, A and B are finite type R-algebras, and A_p and B_q are the local rings at x and y. The finite-type G-ring transfer of Stacks Tag 07PV, recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring], makes A a G-ring, and its localization clause makes A_p a G-ring. The given map is a local map B_q to the p-adic completion of A_p.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, proof, first paragraph; G-ring transfer is More on Algebra Tag 07PV.

proof.text: Choose a presentation B=R[x_1,...,x_n]/(f_1,...,f_m). Let a_i in the completion of A_p be the images of x_i under B to B_q to the completion of A_p. The images in A[x_1,...,x_n] of the f_j vanish at the a_i. Apply [lem-trf-artin-approximation-etale-local-map] with base ring A, prime p, these A-coefficient polynomials, the completed solution (a_i), the G-ring A_p, and N. It gives an etale map A to A', a prime p' over p with kappa(p) to kappa(p') an isomorphism, and b_i in A' solving the same equations with a_i-b_i in (p')^N times the completion of A'_{p'}.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, proof, lines 11049–11063, invoking Smoothing Ring Maps Tag 0CAR.

proof.text: The b_i define an R-algebra map phi:B to A'. For every polynomial h in R[x_1,...,x_n], the difference h(b_1,...,b_n)-h(a_1,...,a_n), after mapping the second term to the completion of A'_{p'}, lies in (p')^N times that completion: expand h into monomials and use that each b_i-a_i lies in this ideal. This gives the congruence for the image under phi of every element represented by a polynomial.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, proof, lines 11054–11060, extending the generator congruences.

proof.text: The induced map on residue fields from the local map B_q to the completion of A_p is injective from kappa(q) into kappa(p). If c is in q, its image under the given map has zero residue; the congruence of Step 3 therefore makes phi(c) have zero residue at p', so phi(c) is in p'. Conversely, if phi(c) is in p', the same congruence makes the image of c under the given local map have zero residue in kappa(p); injectivity on residue fields gives c in q. Hence phi^{-1}(p')=q. This is the required inverse-image equality, not merely the inclusion q subseteq phi^{-1}(p').

source.place: Tag 0CAU, proof, lines 11059–11067, locality at the selected prime.

proof.text: Because phi^{-1}(p')=q, phi localizes to a local map B_q to A'_{p'}. Its contravariant map is an S-morphism f:Spec(A') to Spec(B), and f(p')=q. For a fraction h/s in B_q with s outside q, both evaluations of s are units in the two local rings. The identity (h(b)/s(b))-(h(a)/s(a)) = (h(b)s(a)-h(a)s(b))/(s(b)s(a)), together with the polynomial congruences and the analogous congruence for s, shows that the difference belongs to (p')^N in the completed local ring. Thus the congruence holds for every element of B_q.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, proof, lines 11054–11067, passage from polynomial generators to the localization B_q.

proof.text: The etale ring map A to A' induces an etale morphism p:U=Spec(A') to X=Spec(A), with u=p' mapping to x=p; the residue-field isomorphism is the one supplied in Step 2. The localized map B_q to A'_{p'} gives an S-morphism f:U to Y with f(u)=y. Under the affine identifications, the congruence of Step 5 is exactly that the two completion maps differ by an element of m_u^N times the completed local ring, where m_u=p'A'_{p'}. Shrinking back through the chosen affine opens transports these data to the original schemes and proves the stated conclusion for the arbitrary N.

source.place: Tag 0CAU, conclusion of Tag 0CAU proof at lines 11064–11068.
